newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Woodside says gas reserves 24.4 TCF.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Woodside says gas reserves 24.4 TCF.

text.p: Woodside Petroleum Ltd, operator of Australia's North-West Shelf gas project, said on Monday it has upgraded Shelf reserves to 24.4 trillion cubic feet (tcf) from 15.2 tcf.

"As a result of a highly successful exploration and appraisal programme during 1996 combined with a drive to improve ultimate recovery from existing fields, the total proved raw gas ultimate recovery of the North-West Shelf Gas Project has increased by 60 percent," Woodside said in a statement to the Australian Stock Exchange.
Ultimate probable, including proved, condensate recovery from the North-West Shelf has been increased by 165 million barrels to 894 million barrels, Woodside said.
Ultimate proved condensate recovery has been increased by 122 million barrels to 690 million barrels, the company said.
Woodside said its share of the increase in proved dry gas reserves is 1.4 tcf and 30 million barrels in proved condensate reserves as of December 31, 1996.

"Total proved raw gas ultimate recovery in the North-West Shelf Venture's Production Licence Areas Retention leases and WA-28-P as at December 31, 1996 is put at 24.4 tcf, compared with 15.2 tcf 12 months earlier," Woodside said.
"Probable, including proved, gas ultimate recovery has consequently increased from 18.4 tcf to 27.4 tcf."
Woodside said the bulk of the increase is attributed to successful appraisal wells drilled during 19996 on the Perseus gas field, discovered in 1995.
"Improved gas recovery from the North Rankin field plus new discoveries at Lambert Deep, Searipple and Capella have also significantly contributed to growth in gas resources," it said.
Woodside managing director John Akehurst said the upgrade was the biggest increase in gas resources achieved on the Shelf in any 12-month period.

"The addition to gas ultimate recovery during 1996 was 15 times greater than the net volume of gas produced during the year and almost three times the volume of gas sold during the North West Shelf Project's entire 12 years of operation," he said in a statement.

"The seismic information we now have available gives us confidence that further additions to the total reserves base of the North West Shelf will be made as we continue with our programme of exploration, appraisal and development drilling during 1997 and beyond" he said.
The upgradings come amid negotiations between the joint venture partners and Japanese utilities over vital long term contracts for liquefied natural gas (LNG) with Japanese utilities.
The partners in the project plan to boost LNG capacity to about 14.5 million tonnes from 7.5 million.

Equal partners in the Shelf project are Woodside, The Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd, The British Petroleum Co Plc, Japan Australia LNG (MiMi) Pty Ltd, a partnership of Mitsui & Co Ltd and Mitsubishi Corp, Chevron Corp and Royal Dutch/Shell Group.
